interpretation: Instruction: 'Gently place the red cube on top of the green cube and then open the gripper. Nothing should be dropped from a height.' Robot: capx_robosuite_panda, a 7-DoF Panda with a parallel-jaw gripper (stroke 0.08 m, closing axis TCP x, approach axis TCP z). It has one camera, the scene camera robot0_robotview, and no wrist camera. At the start the green cube (obj1, about 4 cm, rotated about 42 deg about z, top-face centre (0.694, 0.048)) was stacked on top of the red cube (obj2, 4 cm, top -0.071 m, perception labelled it 'brown' because green occluded it). The table is at z = -0.1113 m in the robot-root frame. So this is a restack: green has to come off red and go on the table, then red goes onto green. Goal state: red cube resting on top of green cube, gripper open, and neither cube released from more than a few mm above its support. Nothing in it was ambiguous, apart from how to treat the fact that the gripper started commanded closed (reading 0.79) while holding nothing.
plan: 1) Open the gripper and grasp green top-down with the fingers closing along its face normal (yaw 42.3 deg, the smallest wrist rotation). Grasp high (TCP 1.2 cm below green's top) so the fingertips stay above red's top face. 2) Lift vertically, carry green to a clear spot at (0.62, -0.06) and turn it to yaw 0 on the way so its faces are axis-aligned. Measure the held cube's bottom relative to the TCP from the point cloud, lower it to about 1 mm above the table, release, and lift straight up. 3) Re-measure both cubes from their top faces. Red turned out to be rotated -7.1 deg. Grasp red at yaw -7.1 with the TCP at z = -0.088 (fingertips above the table), lift vertically, carry it over green's measured centre (0.6199, -0.0595) and turn it to yaw 0 so the faces line up. Measure its bottom (2.31 cm below the TCP) and lower it to about 1 mm above green's top (-0.0713). 4) Open, lift vertically, retract toward the robot so the camera sees the stack, and verify. The plan held throughout. The changes were small: a 0.5 s hold to let the gripper finish opening before the first descent, red's grasp yaw corrected from the 0/90 deg first estimated from a partial view to -7.1 deg once it was fully visible, and a re-measurement of green from an unoccluded view before placing red.

steps.what: Read the robot description, the scene camera, objects and 3D views; measured the table (z = -0.1113) with pick() and fitted the cubes' top-face OBBs
steps.why: Identify the cubes and their poses before moving
steps.result: Green (obj1) sat on red (obj2); green's top face 3.9 cm square at yaw 42.3 deg, centre (0.694, 0.048). Red was mostly hidden. Gripper started closed with nothing held (step 0)

steps.what: Moved to a pre-grasp 6.7 cm above green at yaw 42.3, commanding the gripper open; 2.3 s, then a 0.5 s hold
steps.why: Approach from above; the gripper opened slowly (4.2 cm gap after the move), so I waited until it was fully open

steps.what: Descended to TCP z = -0.048 (green top -0.0365, red top -0.0705) and closed the gripper
steps.why: Grip green high enough that the fingertips (about 1-1.5 cm past the TCP) stay above red. check_batch flagged the conservative fingertip spheres; by real geometry they were clear
steps.result: Reading 0.503 (gap 3.98 cm): green held; neither cube disturbed (step 122)

steps.what: Lifted vertically to z = 0.01, then carried green to (0.62, -0.06) turning to yaw 0 (3.3 s)
steps.why: Clear red, then place green at a clear spot with its faces axis-aligned
steps.result: Held green's bottom measured 2.21 cm below the TCP from the cloud; red now fully visible and unmoved (step 188)

steps.what: Lowered green to TCP z = -0.088 (about 1 mm above the table), slowing at the end, then opened and lifted vertically
steps.why: Gentle placement, not dropped from a height
steps.result: Green on the table: top -0.0713, centre (0.6199, -0.0595), yaw 0.0 (step 292)

steps.what: Re-measured red's top face now that it was fully visible
steps.why: My first red estimate came from a partial strip
steps.result: Red centre (0.7037, 0.0483), rotated -7.1 deg, top -0.0713, so both cubes are 4.0 cm tall

steps.what: Moved above red (yaw -7.1, gripper open), re-measured green while it was unoccluded, descended to TCP z = -0.088 and closed
steps.why: Grip red at mid-height with the fingertips above the table

steps.what: Lifted red vertically to z = 0, carried it over green's centre and turned it to yaw 0 (2.9 s)
steps.why: Line red's faces up with green
steps.result: Held red's bottom 2.31 cm below the TCP. Its visible faces (+x 0.6394, +y -0.0396) matched green's (0.6396, -0.0396) (step 448)

steps.what: Lowered red to TCP z = -0.047 (contact expected at -0.0482), the last 2 cm slowly, then opened the gripper
steps.why: Gentle placement on green, released about 1 mm above contact. The fingertip-sphere contacts check_batch flagged against green were sphere artifacts: the real fingertips end about 0.8 cm above red's bottom
steps.result: TCP reached -0.0471; gripper opened to 7.8 cm (step 518)

steps.what: Lifted vertically to z = 0.03, retracted to (0.48, -0.03, 0.12), re-perceived and verified with the camera, a closeup orbit and 3D views
steps.why: Get the gripper out of the camera's view without touching the stack, then check every part of the instruction
steps.result: Red (obj5) top -0.0317, bottom about -0.070; green (obj3) top -0.0713; footprints coincide within about 1 mm. Gripper command 0, reading 0.001. Called finish_episode at step 580 of 1500

diagnosis: I believe the task succeeded. The remaining uncertainty is verification: the robot has only one camera, so the 'two cameras' check was done with that camera plus 3D renders of its depth from other angles. Both releases were made about 1 mm above the estimated contact (from cloud-measured offsets between the TCP and each cube's bottom), so neither cube fell more than a few mm.
lessons: In this robosuite Panda setup the held object drops out of objects(), so check_batch(held='objN') fails with 409. Use held=False, and measure the held cube's bottom relative to the TCP from coloured cloud points instead.
The gripper opens slowly when the command rides on a motion waypoint (only 4.2 cm after a 2.3 s move). Check gripper_gap_m and hold briefly before descending around an object.

Fingertip collision spheres reach about 2.2 cm past the TCP and get flagged against the object being grasped or stacked on. Judge those contacts from the real finger geometry; arm-link contacts would be real.

Measure an occluded object again once it is fully visible: red looked axis-aligned from a partial strip but was rotated -7.1 deg. Fit OBBs to the top-face points of each cube, not to the whole object.
Perception trims about 5 mm above the support plane, so bottom_z reads high. Use top_z and a table pick() for heights (both cubes were 4.0 cm).
Turning a cube about the vertical axis while carrying it is an easy way to line its faces up with the cube underneath.
